3. The actual-Davies release analysis still does not close long HOLD

I investigated the release problem directly in the actual syndrome process, without substituting the classical sampler, a reflected chain, or a circuit-noise oracle.

Let  $Q$  be the Davies syndrome generator,  $\pi$  its Gibbs law, and  $q_a(s)$  the rate of one-site Pauli label  $a$ . A fixed initial Pauli fault supported on  $F$  produces syndrome shift  $u$ .

With

 $(T_uf)(s)=f(s+u),$ the shifted process starts at  $\pi$  and has generator

 $\boxed{Q^u=T_uQT_u,\qquad q_a^u(s)=q_a(s+u).}$ Only labels incident on the changed checks are affected, at most  $c_{\mathrm{inc}}|F|$  of them. Thus an initial local fault is exactly a persistent local generator quench in this analytical frame.

The word “persistent” matters: this representation lasts throughout HOLD. It does not turn the fault into an additional physical intervention.

The path likelihood has a time-occupation cost

On marked trajectories, the exact likelihood ratio is

 $\begin{aligned}
L_t=\exp\Bigg[
&\sum_{a\in A_u}\int_0^t
\log\frac{q_a(X_{v-}+u)}{q_a(X_{v-})}\,dN_a(v)\\
&-\int_0^t\sum_{a\in A_u}
\bigl(q_a(X_v+u)-q_a(X_v)\bigr)\,dv
\Bigg].
\end{aligned}$ The second integral accounts for the time spent at each syndrome. Detailed balance compares a transition with its reverse; it does not remove this term when a defect is translated or deleted from a trajectory.

These marked trajectories are mathematical bookkeeping. No bath record becomes a physically available observation.

For size-independent bounds  $r_-\le q_a(s)\le r_+$ , the derivation gives

 $D(\mathbb P_{Q^u}^{\,t}\Vert\mathbb P_Q^{\,t})
\le
|A_u|t
\left[
r_+\log\frac{r_+}{r_-}-r_++r_-
\right],$ and

 $\mathbb E_Q L_t^2
\le
\exp\!\left[
|A_u|t\frac{(r_+-r_-)^2}{r_-}
\right].$ For fixed  $F$ , these bounds avoid a total-volume factor, but remain extensive in HOLD duration. They identify the cost in this comparison method. They do not say that microscopic trajectory disagreement is logical failure.

Whole-path reversal does cancel the time-occupation factors and gives

 $\Pr_{\mu_0}[X_t\in B]
=
\sum_{b\in B}\pi(b)\,
\mathbb E_b\!\left[
\frac{\mu_0(X_t)}{\pi(X_t)}
\right].$ The remaining expectation is dynamical. Static polymer factorization does not establish the needed cancellation for the evolved observable  $P_t1_B$ .
